fixed: Pali cloud blobs (white, snow-like caps on the Ko'olau crest) are gone. The colour now comes from HLS v2 (Sentinel-2 and Landsat) with its Fmask cloud mask, read from the Microsoft Planetary Computer: 24 summer scenes from 2023-2024, the per-pixel median of cloud-free observations, about 3% of pixels never clear. pali and oahu_nuuanu were both re-baked this way; the windward O'ahu stills show the change.

Pali neon tone: the luminance gain was re-measured on clear O'ahu land with the new composite (0.734; the old composite gave 0.758) and one chroma factor of 0.6 was measured the same way (median MODIS / HLS chroma over 53,000 pixels). Pali land saturation dropped from a median of 0.54 to 0.35 (Maui Nui 0.38), and cloud-white texels from 8.1% to 2.0%.
Pali sea floor: Kane'ohe Bay's shallow sea floor now shows the HLS picture instead of the nearest land's olive colour.

Pali black hillside: the colour texture has no black texels (0.01%). The remaining black in the ground view was the stage's lighting: shade from the sun on a west-facing spur (checked with debug views of albedo, shadow and AO). regions.json pali.film.today now sets sun [75,55] and foamAmt 0.25, which takes near-black from 16.7% to 3.2% (luma 149). I also added an optional slope-relative AO; it only lifts steep faces a little (0.41 to 0.44).
Nihoa: land heights are scaled x1.522 so Millers Peak is 273 m (was 179 m; GNIS 1890767 position; sources give 272-275 m). The coastline is unchanged; regions.json gaps documents the factor.

nwhi_west caps no longer read as snow. The cause was the stage, not the colour texture: the bathtub ring plus the reef shelf covered whole flat caps (cap luma 202, unchanged even with the texture blacked out). New regions.json nwhi_west.film.drained hint (tubAmt 0, reefAmt 0.55) brings the cap to 137 (p95 244 to 195). Sea-floor texels are now coloured by depth, so the Blue Marble cyan is gone. A refill floor of -2 m keeps the atoll tops at -1 to -2 m.

La Perouse Pinnacle is modelled as a 37 m (122 ft, fact ledger) basalt stack. Position -166.2610, 23.7689 is the near-infrared peak in Landsat 8 on 13 Oct 2018 (GNIS gives only the rounded 23 45 N, 166 15 W). It has crags, guano streaks and an irregular reef flat; plan shape, orientation and the smaller second rock are marked approximate. It is 37 m on the lalo grid and in the new 2.5 m region 'laperouse' (stack laperouse > lalo > nwhi_chain).

everest_wide and everest re-baked from the pre-monsoon high-sun window (10 April - 10 June, 2022-2024). Near-black colour texels: everest_wide 6.3% to 0.03% (north faces above 5,000 m 8.6% to 0.07%), everest 3.3% to 0.09%. The baked dark blob is gone. Summer itself was rejected: the monsoon months are cloud-covered and Fmask flags the snowfields as cloud.

East Island 2018 added as dated before/after regions on the lalo grid: lalo_2018_before (Landsat 8, 9 July 2018) and lalo_2018_after (13 Oct 2018, nine days after Walaka). Public-domain USGS Collection 2 via the Planetary Computer. Inside a 0.6 km circle, land is that day's dry sand from near-infrared unmixing: about 33,000 m2 before (published about 11 acres, 45,000 m2) and about 2,700 m2 after (a sliver). Sand that is gone becomes a shoal 2 m down. Staging data only; no number is narrated.
Found and fixed: lalo's AO had been 80% zeros since round 2 (a float64 grid misread by Image.fromarray 'F'). The grid is now float32 before the AO step. The GIBS probe now survives an error page.

Recorded every change in regions.json (gaps, film hints, facts, dated entries via make_index.py), regions_spec.json, lab/hawaii/README.md (new bake options), PLAYBOOK_production section 15 DO/DONT and LESSONS_LOG. result.notes:
Nothing was committed, pushed, published or posted. I only edited the toolkit and lab files, the test page, the docs and the new img/tools files. The narration, script, sound files and chN.js were not touched.

(1) Globe (cineglobe.js and shared.js)
- The "cloud seam" was not a single seam. There were three faults:
  - The cloud map's own date-line edge drifts with the clouds to lon 180 - 0.04t. A test at film time 500 s showed it as a hard vertical edge at 160 E. Fix: the drift now starts 60 deg on, so the seam stays between 120 E and 90 E, behind the limb of every Hawaiian shot. It is also cross-faded over 3 deg either side with the map shifted half a world, and fract() is gone from the cloud UV, because it caused a mip hairline.
  - The day texture's dark ocean has 16x16 JPEG macroblocks. These showed as squares west of Hawaii, the "seam" in the earlier round-2 still (renders with clouds 0 proved they came from the day texture, not the clouds).
  - The texture paints bathymetry into the ocean, which made the cyan-white shelf smears.
  Fix for both texture faults: open water now reads mip 4 (one texel per macroblock), and brightness above the deep ocean is compressed 85% toward a muted teal. Coasts and land are untouched. STORY globe luma is 95.9 (was 96.4), with no squares and no glow.
- Side fix: the HERO preset measured luma 49-56 on an oblique. I raised its exposure 1.83x, and it now measures 87-91.
- Weak point: without the shelf glow, islands sit on plain blue, so outlines and labels carry them on wide globes.

(2) scaleMove (shared.js)
- Globe and terrain legs share one log-altitude orbit path. At the 900 km hand-off, the two legs rendered alone line up within about 10-15 px; the globe's coasts are 5 km texels. There is no double image.
- Terrain legs blend their water toward a navy ocean between 25 and 500 km. Without this, film water seen from orbit renders as saturated teal (red channel about 0) and the ocean flipped colour at the hand-off. Ocean colour across the dissolve: (88,111,156) -> (69,100,152) -> (38,89,146), luma 96 -> 96 -> 83. The teal returns below about 60 km.
- The log warns if the region stack does not cover the hand-off view.
- I did not convert any existing xfade in the chapters.

(3) Paper kit
- Nine PD cut-outs, every one logged with page, original and edits in img/SOURCES.md:
  - Tourist: LOC FSA 1939, Russell Lee, "Man with luggage", LOC 2017740557. Hand-tinted, with a drawn cream flower print on a red shirt. The hat is a separate part (the head under it is painted as plain dark hair), and his Gladstone bag is the suitcase.
  - Jeep: LOC FSA/OWI 2017872210. It is a military jeep with cadets in helmets.
  - USFWS monk seal and pup.
  - USFWS Laysan albatross, standing and in flight.
  - NPS Denali climber. He is an unnamed, modern volunteer, cut at the knees and carried by the base tab. He wears a jacket, not the down suit and oxygen mask the script asks for.
- Procedural props: COMING SOON sign, plain orange pennant, water drop, envelope with no writing, '?' tag, water tank.
- drawCutout gives each figure a contact shadow and a cast shadow from the stage sun, a base tab, pop-up, lean, wobble, paper turn and the detachable hat.
- The Commons originals returned HTTP 429, so the seal, albatross and climber come from 960 px renditions. The source figures are 300-450 px tall and slightly soft. The pup is a small dark shape.
- The IS-Net model was deleted after use (it was never in the repo).
- I did not add a codebreakers or radio-room cut-out, because the script draws those beats as glyph streams.

(4) section.js
- The volcanic pile is now the light band, the crust the dark slate band, and the mantle a mid olive green. Everest's slab was lifted so it stays lighter than the pile.
- Payoff luma is 112-118 with near-black at 3.6% or less. All three bands read on the 390 px sheet.

- Luma on the final stills: cast 120-128, move 83-120, globe 97-107.
- ch1 frames 0 and 95 render as before (luma 97.6).
- No AI wording on screen.
